purpose: Structural layout primitive for scrolling regions: native overflow with themed thin scrollbars and keyboard scrolling. With `fade`, the edges that still have content to scroll to fade out, each sized by the distance left on that side (capped at 64px or a sixth of the viewport), so a list reads as continuing past its frame. A sticky header inside the viewport keeps its full opacity; the top fade starts below it.
useWhen: A region that must scroll inside a bounded box: a navigation list, a panel body, a wide table (`orientation="horizontal"`), a code region (`orientation="both"`).
A long list whose edges should fade while more content lies beyond them (`fade`).
avoidWhen: The region is one of several the reader resizes by dragging → use `resizable`, with a ScrollArea inside a pane if its content overflows.
It is an application navigation rail → use `sidebar`, which already scrolls its items.
It is a code sample → use `code-block`, which already scrolls its lines.
related: sidebar` — scrolls its navigation inside a built-in ScrollArea.
code-block` — runs its code lines in a ScrollArea with `orientation="both"`.
resizable` — draggable regions; each pane can hold a ScrollArea.
bestPractices: Give it a bounded height, or a flex parent that constrains it. Without a limit the content never overflows and nothing scrolls.
The root is focusable (`tabindex` 0) and scrolls with the arrow keys, Page Up/Down and Home/End. Set `aria-label` when no visible heading names the region.
Pass `tabindex="-1"` only when the content is itself focusable and keyboard users can already reach all of it.
Match `orientation` to the overflow axis: `vertical` clips horizontal overflow, and `horizontal` clips vertical overflow.
